title: Seltos and Sonet built Kia in India. Can hybrid and CNG power its next growth phase?- Moneycontrol.com
text:

Kia is betting on hybrid and CNG models to strengthen growth as its market share remains below the FY23 peak.   September 15, 2026 / 13:18 IST             Kia began selling cars in India in August 2019, building its presence around the Seltos SUV. The Sonet SUV followed in September 2020 and became another strong volume driver. Seven years later, the company has a much wider portfolio, but its next challenge is different -- growing faster than the passenger vehicle (PV) market and finding another product or powertrain combination that can deliver volumes at scale. Atul Sood, Senior Vice President, Sales and Marketing, Kia India, told Moneycontrol in an interaction that the company expects its existing models, new powertrains and wider semi-urban reach to support the next phase of growth. "We have got a very good response for the new Seltos that we had introduced in December last year," he said, adding that the Sonet continues to do very well. Kia's sales to dealers increased from 84,903 units in FY20 to 1,55,686 units in FY21 and 1,86,787 units in FY22. Sales then jumped to 2,69,229 units in FY23. The momentum weakened after that. Sales declined 8.76 per cent year-on-year to 2,45,634 units in FY24 and increased only 3.90 per cent to 2,55,207 units in FY25. Kia returned to stronger growth in FY26, recording its highest-ever domestic sales of 2,89,035 units, up 13.26 per cent year-on-year. The Sonet SUV was its largest-selling model during the year with 1,14,142 units, followed by the Seltos SUV at 83,747 units and the Carens MPV at 76,837 units. Together, the three models accounted for around 95 per cent of Kia's domestic sales. However, Kia's domestic PV market share stood at 6.22 per cent in FY26, lower than its FY23 peak of 6.92 per cent. Between FY23 and FY26, the company's volumes grew 7.36 per cent, while the overall PV industry in India expanded at a much faster pace of 19.37 per cent. The trend continued in Q1 FY27. Kia's wholesales rose 19.32 per cent year-on-year to 79,424 units, but the industry posted a higher growth rate of 25.89 per cent. Consequently, the company's market share declined to 6.24 per cent from 6.58 per cent in the year-ago period. Sood pointed out that Kia was deliberately not pushing vehicles into dealerships merely to increase wholesale numbers. "We are not pushing wholesales," he said, adding that the company wants to ensure that its dealers are also sustainable. He noted that the retail picture was stronger, with Kia's January-August registrations on Vahan growing by more than 24 per cent, compared with the industry's 19 per cent growth. Kia's portfolio currently includes the Sonet, Syros, Seltos and Sorento SUVs; Carens, Carens Clavis and Carnival MPVs; and the Syros EV, Carens Clavis EV, EV6 and EV9 electric vehicles. Despite this spread, petrol vehicles presently contribute 61 per cent to the company's volumes, followed by diesel at 38 per cent and EVs at 1 per cent. Until its latest introductions, Kia had no presence in CNG or hybrid vehicles. The industry's powertrain mix is more diverse. In Q1 FY27, petrol accounted for 52 per cent of PV sales, followed by CNG at 23 per cent, diesel at 18 per cent, electric at 5 per cent and hybrid at 2 per cent, according to SIAM. Earlier this month, Kia launched the three-row Sorento SUV with a hybrid powertrain, becoming the first Korean carmaker in India to offer one. Although Hyundai has announced its hybrid plans, it has not launched a hybrid model yet. The company also introduced factory-fitted CNG options in the Carens and Carens Clavis. A dealer-installed CNG option was previously available for the Carens. "This one comes factory-fitted, with our quality and warranty," Sood said. According to industry data, CNG contributes 70 per cent to the combined sales of the Ertiga, XL6 and Rumion -- the three direct rivals of the Carens and Carens Clavis. "CNG is now becoming a customer preference across segments," he said. "They are looking for frugality, more fuel economy," he added. The company is also viewing hybrids as a wider strategy rather than a powertrain limited to the Sorento. "We are not looking at hybrids only for Sorento. It is a powertrain we are focussed on," he observed. With prices starting at Rs 27,99,000 (ex-showroom), the Sorento operates in a lower-volume premium segment, but gives existing Kia customers an upgrade option. The carmaker also expects to attract buyers currently outside the brand, although Sood declined to provide a volume target for the SUV. "So, what is the next option for them? We want to give them a very good option," he said, referring to existing Kia customers. Kia is targeting minimum domestic sales of 4,10,000 units and a market share of 7.6 percent by 2030. Its Anantapur plant currently has an annual production capacity of around 4,30,000 units. Sood said the existing capacity was adequate for now. However, since the domestic target does not include exports, further expansion will eventually be required. "It will necessitate expansion for sure," he added.
